The next step should test whether earlier ordering improves target ranking after controlling for the final item. At 10% research progress, this is a feasible extension of the supplied GRU4Rec diagnostic.

### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Existing execution checks establish whether temporal interventions are interpretable. Padding invariance and final-nonpadding readout must remain prerequisites. (2) Fixed candidates make within-user rank differences comparable. Training-prefix results nevertheless remain conditional, in-sample evidence. (3) Feedback suggests recent, repeated behavior may be underused, but neither histories nor simulator feedback establishes current ownership or intent. Measure temporal utility without assigning those latent explanations.

**Related-work insights.** (1) *Does It Look Sequential?* motivates shuffled-history controls and uncertainty estimates: sensitivity alone does not establish useful ordering. (2) *Repeated Padding* motivates checking padding behavior before attributing changes to memory. (3) *Improved Estimation of Ranks* cautions that sampled candidates affect ranking estimates; diagnostic candidate sets must remain fixed and must not replace the pinned evaluator.

These insights define three directions: execution fidelity, controlled temporal attribution, and evidence-bounded interpretation.

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal attribution | Shuffle earlier items while fixing the final item | 4: useful control combination; established perturbation technique | 7: inexpensive, reusable evidence; limited mechanistic resolution | 2: existing hooks suffice; needs careful pairing |
| Memory localization | Reset hidden state before an identical recent suffix | 6: sharper memory intervention; related to standard ablation | 7: localizes prefix dependence; reset states can be atypical | 6: replay is practical; exact GRU implementation access required |
| Attribution triangulation | Compare positional integrated gradients with deletions | 4: established attribution combination; little methodological novelty | 6: checks attribution agreement; correlated inputs complicate interpretation | 5: automatic differentiation helps; baselines and batching require care |

### Selected idea: final-item-controlled temporal utility

For each existing eligible training-prefix example, evaluate the original history, five permutations of all earlier items with the final item fixed, and the existing last-item-only control. Preserve sequence membership, target, candidate identities, and padding placement. Use seed 42 and actual model scores, including biases.

Compute paired target-rank damage and HR@10 damage. Degradation after shuffling supports useful earlier-order dependence conditional on the final item. Similarity to last-item-only performance is consistent with a shortcut, but cannot establish one by itself. Report category-specific user-bootstrap intervals, counts, and length slices; do not treat a nonsignificant difference as equivalence.

Implement this inside the existing probe, retaining its interfaces, RNG restoration, execution checks, and metric definitions. No model retraining or predictor change is required. Each category retains exactly one GRU4Rec checkpoint. Only the host’s four-category macro validation HR@10 selects training changes; these measurements guide subsequent hypotheses.

idea.description: Add a paired temporal-utility probe that permutes earlier history items while fixing the final item, using the existing original-history and last-item-only controls on the same trained GRU4Rec checkpoint.
idea.motivation: The supplied probe already measures broad perturbation sensitivity. Fixing the final item isolates whether earlier ordering contributes useful target-ranking information beyond immediate recency, directly addressing the feedback hypothesis without inferring unobserved user intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Reuse existing training-prefix examples and frozen target-plus-99-negative candidate sets; do not access hidden evaluation files. Require passing execution checks. Permute only nonpadding items preceding the final item, keeping left padding intact. Obtain features through view.log2feats and scores through view.predict_score; read the maximum nonzero position and skip empty histories. Average five permutations within each user before bootstrapping users. Report rank damage as perturbed rank minus original rank and HR damage as original hit minus perturbed hit. Use the existing minimum of 30 complete users for intervals, otherwise return null with a reason. Preserve model mode and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states. Training remains seed 42, preprocessing seed 0, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Retain routing across all four categories, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. This diagnostic does not modify the trained architecture or embedded predictor.
idea.pseudocode:
def final_item_controlled_probe(view, examples, device):
    # Called within the existing RNG-preserving, eval-mode diagnosis context.
    rng = numpy.random.default_rng(42)
    outcomes = []
    for example in examples:
        sequence, target, candidates = example  # Existing frozen training-prefix case.
        positions = nonzero_positions(sequence)
        if len(positions) < 5:
            continue
        def rank_and_hit(seq):
            features = view.log2feats(seq[None].to(device))
            last = maximum_nonzero_position(seq)
            state = features[:, last, :]
            scores = view.predict_score(state, candidates.to(device))
            return existing_target_rank_and_hit(scores, target, candidates, k=10)
        original_rank, original_hit = rank_and_hit(sequence)
        repetitions = []
        for _ in range(5):
            altered = sequence.clone()
            earlier = positions[:-1]
            permutation = rng.permutation(len(earlier))
            altered[earlier] = sequence[earlier[permutation]]
            rank, hit = rank_and_hit(altered)
            repetitions.append((rank - original_rank, original_hit - hit))
        outcomes.append(mean_within_user(repetitions))
    return paired_user_summary_with_bootstrap(outcomes, minimum_users=30)
# Integrate measured outputs and definitions into the existing diagnosis result.
# Compare alongside the existing last-item-only control; never select models by this probe.

originality.positive: Combines final-item control with paired ranking utility and existing execution checks in a focused GRU4Rec diagnostic.
originality.negative: Shuffled-history controls and recency ablations are established methods; this is an incremental diagnostic extension.

future_potential.positive: Provides inexpensive evidence for deciding whether later work should target earlier-order learning or immediate-recency reliance.
future_potential.negative: In-sample sampled-candidate effects cannot establish generalization, causal intent, or the internal mechanism responsible.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing feature, scoring, candidate, and bootstrap interfaces without accessing GRU internals.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct pairing, tie handling, padding preservation, and user-level aggregation require care.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (RecSys 2024)
contributions: Motivates original-versus-shuffled history comparisons and bootstrap uncertainty for temporal utility.
limitations: Order sensitivity does not by itself establish useful temporal reasoning or explain user intent.

related_work.title: Repeated Padding (2024)
contributions: Shows that padding strategy can materially affect GRU4Rec behavior.
limitations: Does not establish that a particular perturbation effect represents forgetting or useful memory.

related_work.title: Improved Estimation of Ranks for Learning Item Recommenders with Negative Sampling (2024)
contributions: Documents challenges in rank estimation under negative sampling.
limitations: Fixed diagnostic candidates ensure paired comparability but do not remove sampled-ranking bias.

related_work.title: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
contributions: Introduces integrated gradients, supporting the proposed attribution-triangulation alternative.
limitations: Attributions depend on the baseline and do not establish causal relevance or ranking utility.
